text: He is not breathing and I cannot find a pulse.
rationale: MARCH: respiration absent. Highest priority regardless of other findings.

text: Blood is spurting from his thigh in time with his heartbeat.
rationale: MARCH: massive haemorrhage, arterial. Pulsatile flow is the arterial marker.

text: She has a third degree burn across most of her back.
rationale: Full-thickness burn over a large body surface area.

text: His arm has an open fracture, the bone has broken the skin.
rationale: Open fracture: stabilisation and evacuation, not immediately life-threatening.

text: Just a small cut on my thumb from a knife.
rationale: Superficial laceration, basic first aid sufficient.

text: The wound has swelling and a red streak running up from it.
rationale: Lymphangitis, signs of infection. Needs monitoring, not urgent intervention.

text: The bleeding hasn't stopped, it is still pouring out.
rationale: Haemorrhage explicitly ongoing. The word 'stopped' appears but is negated.

text: The bleeding has stopped now after I applied pressure.
rationale: Haemorrhage controlled. Downgraded from critical, still shock risk.

text: It has not stopped bleeding at all.
rationale: Full-form negation of the same cue.

text: I'm not sure, but the bleeding has stopped.
rationale: The negation attaches to 'sure', not to 'stopped'. Contrast word resets scope.

text: The bleeding stopped but then started again and is still going.
rationale: Re-escalation in a later clause overrides the earlier resolution.

text: It was bleeding badly but not anymore, all clear now.
rationale: Resolved haemorrhage. Not minor: recent significant blood loss.

text: Bleeding has not really stopped, it just slowed a little.
rationale: Hedged negation. Flow continues.

text: The bleeding hasn't continued, it stopped right after we packed it.
rationale: An earlier unrelated negation must not carry onto the later affirmed 'stopped'.

text: He is not breathing and there is a small cut that stopped bleeding.
rationale: Airway/respiration outranks a resolved minor laceration.

text: She twisted her ankle and blood is pumping out of her calf.
rationale: Massive haemorrhage outranks a sprain.

text: He has a scrape on his knee and has been confused since hitting his head.
rationale: Altered mental state after head trauma outranks a graze.

text: There is a bruise on his shin and a splinter in his palm.
rationale: Two minor findings; the most urgent is still minor.

text: His lips have gone blue and his chest is not moving at all.
rationale: Cyanosis with absent chest rise is respiratory arrest, described without the word 'breathing'.

text: There is a pool of blood under her and it keeps getting bigger.
rationale: Ongoing uncontrolled haemorrhage, described without 'spurting' or 'hasn't stopped'.

text: His skin is cold and clammy, he's grey and his heart is racing.
rationale: Classic compensated shock, described without the word 'shock'.

text: She cannot feel her legs since she fell off the ladder.
rationale: Possible spinal cord injury, described without 'spine' or 'fracture'.

text: The cut is clean, the edges sit together and nothing is coming out.
rationale: Superficial and haemostatic, described without 'small cut'.

text: He has been in the water for hours, is shaking hard and making no sense.
rationale: Hypothermia with altered mentation, described without the word 'hypothermia'.
